brief.headline: Cut our laminate bill by ₹32.69 L/yr by matching the ₹290.00/KG we already pay Shrinath, and shorten payment to 15 days in return for a 2% discount.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹290.00/KG across the top three SKUs where we overpay
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹290.00/KG to Shrinath Roto Pack for the same laminates — GEEP charges ₹294.03 to ₹308.30/KG on those items. The open-market asking price for pharma ORS sachet laminate sits at ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), so our current price is at the top edge of fair; pushing to ₹290.00/KG keeps us inside the band and aligns with our best internal price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (cut our term from 30 to 15) in exchange for a 2% price cut on top of the ₹290.00/KG
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹1.16 Cr of our cash, but their cash is stuck for 81 days (longer than similar firms at 46 days), so early payment is worth real money to them — they borrow at about 4.38%, so two weeks early is worth roughly 0.4%, but we ask for 2% to make the trade attractive to us.

brief.financialLeverage: They sell ₹291.36 Cr a year and keep only ₹1.1 of every ₹100 as profit (peers keep ₹2.1). Our ₹28.31 Cr is 9.72% of everything they sell — we're a big customer they can't afford to lose. Their cash is stuck for 81 days, much longer than similar firms (46 days), so they'll value faster payment. But with profit so thin, a huge price cut could hurt their ability to supply us — so we push hardest on payment terms and only a modest price move to our best internal benchmark. Their rating is CRISIL BB+ / Stable, but the agency did it without their help, so treat their health as uncertain and line up a backup.

evidence.point: We overpay by ₹32.69 L/yr versus the ₹290.00/KG we pay Shrinath
Our spend is 9.72% of their total sales — we're a major customer
They keep only ₹1.1 of every ₹100 they sell, half what similar firms keep
Their cash is stuck for 81 days, much longer than peers at 46 days
Paying them 15 days faster frees ₹1.16 Cr of our cash
They supply 76% of our Laminates (₹28.31 Cr) — we're heavily dependent on them

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd (already a tiny FDC supplier)
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter with ₹2611.64 Cr revenue — proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets; already supplies us in small volumes so onboarding risk is low.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant (₹16492.00 Cr revenue) that makes both the film substrate and converts it — can second-source GEEP at scale if they stumble.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, does pharma blister and sachet laminates (₹222.04 Cr revenue) — strong technical fit as a backup for GEEP.

risks: They supply 76% of our Laminates (₹28.31 Cr in annual spend) — we have almost no backup if they can't deliver; qualify a second source before pushing too hard.
Their rating (CRISIL BB+ / Stable) was done without their cooperation, so the agency's view may be stale — treat their financial health as uncertain.
They have GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and pending legal cases — these are red flags for operational or cash trouble.
Profit is only 1.1% — pushing a big price cut could tip them into losses and threaten our supply; focus the squeeze on payment terms and a modest price move to ₹290.00/KG.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹294 to ₹308 per kilo when we know ₹290 is achievable — let's talk about how we close that gap and how faster payment from us can help your cash flow.
